title: Introduce iterative RAG authoring shell quickstart (watch mode, incremental index)
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: - Add iterative RAG authoring shell quickstart: local-first watch mode, incremental indexer, live assertions, and telemetry presets for dev workflows.
body: Summary: Add a compact, local-first quickstart (iterative-authoring-shell) aimed at improving developer feedback loops when building retrieval-augmented generation workflows. This quickstart provides a lightweight devcontainer, a file-watcher incremental indexer, a small CLI shim for starting sessions, and an assertions harness for stepwise checks. Motivation: Teams repeatedly ask for a minimal authoring loop that mirrors production RAG behavior (incremental indexing, short feedback iterations, deterministic assertions) without the overhead of a full orchestration stack. This quickstart targets engineers who want to iterate on prompts, index changes, and tooling bindings quickly and reproducibly. What this PR adds: - quickstarts/iterative-authoring-shell/: new directory with README.md, sample corpus, docker/devcontainer, example prompts and assertion suite. - authoring-cli/authoring.sh: tiny cross-platform shim to start a local watcher and an ephemeral Redis-backed index for tests. - telemetry-presets.json: minimal telemetry probe config for the Console to pick up session traces. - examples/recipes/stepwise-assertions.json: example assertion sets and step expectations. - CI: docsite integration and a smoke e2e which exercises the watch flow. Compatibility notes: - Uses the same Redwood API surface as other quickstarts; no breaking API changes. - The watch indexer defaults to a memory-backed index for local runs; instructions included for switching to a persistent index or cloud vector DB. Usage (short): 1) git clone && cd quickstarts/iterative-authoring-shell 2) ./authoring.sh up (spins devcontainer / watcher / local index) 3) edit samples/content/*.md and observe incremental index updates and live re-runs of assertions 4) ./authoring.sh run-eval to run the sample assertion set Checklist: - [x] Add scaffold and README with step-by-step authoring loop - [x] Implement watch-mode indexer with debouncing and basic dedupe - [x] Add lightweight authoring CLI shim - [x] Provide telemetry presets and example traces - [x] Add smoke CI job that runs the local flow in ephemeral mode - [x] Tests: small integration smoke that validates incremental index and tiny prompt-generated output Open items (post-merge): - Link the quickstart to the docs site quickstart index (DOCS- follow-up) - Add optional integration example for a customer-managed vector DB (community contribution) Commits summary: - init: scaffold iterative-authoring-shell quickstart (README, samples, devcontainer) - add: authoring CLI and memory-backed incremental indexer - add: stepwise assertions and example recipes - ci: add smoke e2e and docsite checks - fix: adjust debounce window and error handling for file watch - docs: expand README with troubleshooting and switching to persistent index CI observations: initial CI run failed the smoke e2e due to a 1s debounce race; fixed in follow-up commit and rerun; final CI status: all checks passed. Merge: Squash-and-merge to main with a concise commit message referencing ENG-1249 and PM-881.

review_thread: Jordan Lee: Nice compact quickstart. Can we keep the devcontainer optional? Some contributors prefer not to use Docker during quick iterations.
Maya Patel: Yes — devcontainer is opt-in. README updated with 'local-only' instructions; added ./authoring.sh up --no-container flag.
Shaan Mehta: Watcher seems good, but can we reduce noisy logs during large corpora? Suggest silencing INFO lines and exposing verbosity flag.
Maya Patel: Added a --quiet flag and switched to debounced INFO->DEBUG default for filewatch logging.
Lina Torres: Can we add a sample assertion that demonstrates a deliberate failure so authors learn how the harness surfaces regressions?
Maya Patel: Added failing-example.md + assertion to examples/recipes for educational purposes.
Jordan Lee: CI flaked on smoke-e2e due to timing — resolved after debounce increase. Approving.
Shaan Mehta: Approved after small logging change.
ci_checks: smoke-e2e: fail -> rerun -> pass (initial debounce race)
merge_details: Merged via squash (squash-and-merge). Merge commit: 'introduce iterative rag authoring shell quickstart (ENG-1249, PM-881)'.
notes: This quickstart intentionally uses a memory-backed index by default to keep feedback loops sub-second on typical laptops.
Telemetry presets are minimal; they intentionally avoid sampling production traffic. They are intended for developer sessions only.
Follow-up: add a 'connect-to-vector-db' guide for persistent index usage; suggested as a community contribution.
